evidence.title: Dashboard FAQ
evidence.text:
If you've just installed Plausible and aren't seeing your own visits, there are a few common reasons:

- **WordPress plugin**: Our official WordPress plugin excludes logged-in admin visits by default. If the verification tool confirms the tracking is working, you have nothing to worry about.
- **Shields**: The Shields feature lets you block visits based on IP addresses, hostnames, countries or specific pages. Check whether you have any rules that might be excluding your own visits.
- **Adblockers**: If you're using a browser extension or network-level adblocker, it may be blocking the Plausible script. Consider setting up a proxy to serve the script as a first-party connection.

For more details, see our full troubleshooting guide.

evidence.title: Adding Plausible to WordPress
evidence.text: Our WordPress plugin excludes logged-in administrator visits by default. This is intentional. If you want to track your own visits, go to the "Track analytics for user roles" section in the plugin settings and enable the Administrator role.

question: I bought as a company and need our address and VAT ID on the invoices, but I already paid. Can I add it now?
reference_answer: Yes, open any invoice from Paddle and click Add address & VAT Number. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on, but invoices already issued stay as they were. With a valid VAT ID no VAT is charged on future payments, except for UK businesses, which still pay UK VAT they can reclaim.

Details appear on invoices from then on; already-issued invoices stay as they were
No VAT on future payments with a valid VAT ID
UK businesses still pay UK VAT

evidence.title: View and save your invoices
evidence.text:
Our payment processor Paddle sends an invoice by email automatically after each payment. You can also view past invoices from your Plausible account. Paddle doesn't issue credit notes or receipts for refunds, so a refund has no separate document.

Log in to your Plausible account. In the top right menu, click your account name and open the settings. Scroll down in the **Subscription** section to see a list of all invoices. Select an invoice to open it in a new browser tab.

To save a PDF copy, use your browser's **Print** command and select **Save as PDF** as the destination.

Invoice list in Plausible settings

## Add your company address and VAT number

Open any invoice from Paddle and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Paddle handles VAT and sales taxes. If you provide a valid VAT ID, no VAT will be charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. When Paddle refunds the VAT on a payment after accepting your VAT number, it doesn't send a separate credit note. Instead, it reissues that payment's invoice without VAT, and the reissued invoice is the one for your records. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

## Change your billing address

Open any invoice and click **Edit business address** to update your address.

Changing the **country** on an existing subscription isn't possible due to tax regulations. To switch countries, cancel your subscription a day or two before your next renewal, then subscribe again right away from the same account with the new country (see How do I change the country on my subscription?). No data is lost in this process.

evidence.title: Billing FAQ
evidence.text:
If you're purchasing on behalf of a business, click **Add VAT number** on the second step of the checkout, where you also add your payment details. Paddle handles all sales tax calculations and will apply the correct rate based on your details.

Add VAT number at checkout

If you missed this step, open your most recent Paddle invoice and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Once Paddle accepts a valid VAT number, no VAT is charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

Paddle checks EU VAT numbers against the EU's VIES database. If your number shows as invalid, check it there first: a number that isn't registered in VIES for trade between EU countries can't be accepted, even when it's valid in your own country.

question: Can I get bounce rate for each goal in a single API query?
reference_answer: No. Mixing the session metrics bounce_rate, views_per_visit and visit_duration with event dimensions such as event:goal isn't allowed. The only exceptions are event:page, and event:hostname when it is used together with event:page.
key_facts: Session metrics can't be mixed with event dimensions
bounce_rate, views_per_visit and visit_duration are session metrics
Exceptions are event:page and event:hostname with event:page
answer: Currently, it is only possible to break down on one property at a time [1]. Using a list of properties with one query is not supported [1].

citations.quote: Currently, it is only possible to break down on one property at a time.
Using a list of properties with one query is not supported.

evidence.title: Stats API v1 reference (legacy)
evidence.text: Currently, it is only possible to break down on one property at a time. Using a list of properties with one query is not supported. So if you want a breakdown by both `event:page` and `visit:source` for example, you would have to make multiple queries (break down on one property and filter on another) and then manually/programmatically group the results together in one report. This also applies for breaking down by time periods. To get a daily breakdown for every page, you would have to break down on `event:page` and make multiple queries for each date. For a simple time period breakdown, have a look at the Timeseries endpoint.

question: how many ip adresses can i block in plausible? my office has like 40 diffrent ones
reference_answer: You can block up to 30 different IP addresses per website, and you add them one at a time as full IP addresses because IP ranges aren't supported.
key_facts: Up to 30 IP addresses per website
One full IP address at a time
IP ranges are not supported
answer: You can block up to 30 different IP addresses per website [1].

citations.quote: You can block up to 30 different IP addresses per website

evidence.title: Exclude internal traffic from your analytics
evidence.text:
* Go into the site settings of the website you'd like to block your activity from

* Choose **IP Addresses** in the **Shields** entry in the left-hand menu

* Click on the **Add IP Address** button to add a new address to the block list

* You can manually insert an IP address (both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are acceptable) or you can click to block your current public IP address which our system will find and display for you

Plausible Shields modal to add an IP address to the block list with a description

* You can also add a description to help you identify which device or location you have blocked

* You need to add one IP address at a time and it has to be the full IP address as IP ranges are not supported. You can block up to 30 different IP addresses per website

Note: Block both IPv4 and IPv6 if your device uses both
Most modern devices and networks have both an IPv4 address (e.g. `203.0.113.5`) and an IPv6 address (e.g. `2001:db8::1`). Your browser or network proxy may send visits using either one depending on the connection.

If you block only your IPv4 address but your browser sends a request over IPv6, that visit will still be recorded. To reliably exclude your traffic, check whether your device has both address types and add each one separately.

The **block your current IP** button captures whichever address your browser is currently using. Click it, then visit a site like whatismyipaddress.com to check whether you also have a second address type, and add that manually if so.

* Once added to the block list, we will start blocking traffic from that specific IP address within a few minutes

* You can see the list of all the IP addresses that you're blocking at the moment. The entry in the list which has the **YOU** tag is your current IP address

* You can click the trash icon next to that IP address to remove it from the blocklist

* You can click the trash icon next to that IP address to remove it from the blocklist

Plausible Shields IP block list with three blocked IP addresses

question: My Top Pages list shows /pricing and /pricing/ as two separate rows. How do I merge them?
reference_answer: The best fix is a 301 redirect so each page has a single address. If you can't change how your site handles URLs, you can merge them in your snippet with a `transformRequest` function that removes the trailing slash. It only affects pageviews sent after you add it, and you should update any pageview goal that ends with a slash.

question: i'm sending events from my backend and getting a 202 back but nothing shows up in my dashboard. what's going on?
reference_answer: The Events API returns 202 even when it drops an event, so check the response headers for x-plausible-dropped: 1, which means bot filtering rejected it. The most common cause is X-Forwarded-For containing a server or CDN IP instead of the real visitor IP. You can send a test request with the X-Debug-Request: true header to see which IP Plausible sees.
key_facts: API always returns HTTP 202 even when dropped
x-plausible-dropped: 1 header means rejected by bot filtering
Common cause is a server or CDN IP in X-Forwarded-For
X-Debug-Request: true shows the IP used
answer: The Events API returns 202 Accepted even when an event is dropped, usually because `X-Forwarded-For` carries a server IP instead of the visitor's [1]. Sending an event from your site is not enough, as you must also create a matching goal in your site settings under **Goals** [2].

citations.quote: The Events API returns 202 Accepted even when an event is dropped, usually because `X-Forwarded-For` carries a server IP instead of the visitor's.
